mainTopic: The father's rights over his daughter (earnings, נדרים, גט, produce) and the husband's rights to her dowry
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a father gets the things his daughter finds so there will be no bad feeling (איבה). It then asks where we learn that her earnings (מעשה ידיה) belong to her father. רב הונא in the name of רב learns it from the פסוק about selling a daughter as an אמה. The גמרא asks whether this covers only a קטנה, whom he can sell, and not a נערה. A logical proof from the father's right to marry her off is knocked down by רב אחאי. In the end the גמרא shows that a קטנה needs no פסוק, so the פסוק must be teaching about a נערה. Next, the גמרא gives the sources for the father cancelling her נדרים and receiving her גט. Then it explains a dispute about whether a father eats the produce of her property, which turns on whether he needs that reward to ransom her. Last, it brings a dispute about a promised dowry when a bride dies during אירוסין, and starts comparing it to the argument of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the Rabbis; that comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The father gets her found items to prevent bad feeling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer: the father gets his daughter's found items because of איבה, bad feeling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of bad feeling.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a discussion from just before: why a daughter's found items (מציאה) go to her father. The answer is so there will be no bad feeling between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's right to her מציאה does not come from a פסוק. It is a rabbinic rule meant to keep peace at home. If she kept what she found, he might resent her and become reluctant to support her.

phrases.english: Because of bad feeling.
phrases.notes: This answers the question just before this point: why the father gets the things his daughter finds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion about the father's right to his daughter's found items.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father gets her מציאה so that there will be no resentment between them.

steps.title: Where do we learn that her earnings go to the father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, the father's right to her earnings, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the father is entitled to her earnings. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the משנה, the father's right to his daughter's earnings, and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Found items were explained by a practical reason (איבה). For earnings, the גמרא expects a real source in the Torah, so it asks מנלן.

keyTerms.meaning: her earnings; literally, the work of her hands
from where do we know this?

phrases.english: To her earnings.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה: the father is entitled to his daughter's earnings.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from found items to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that a daughter's earnings belong to her father.

steps.title: Learned from the daughter sold as a maidservant
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of רב learns it from the פסוק about a father selling his daughter as an אמה: just as an אמה's earnings go to her master, a daughter's earnings go to her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: From where do we know that a daughter's earnings belong to her father? The פסוק says, 'If a man sells his daughter as a maidservant.' Just as a maidservant's earnings belong to her master, so a daughter's earnings belong to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the source. He compares a daughter to an אמה, a maidservant, because the Torah mentions them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lets a father sell his daughter as an אמה, and the master gets her work. The פסוק puts a daughter side by side with an אמה: just as the master gets the אמה's work, the father gets his daughter's work. (The reasoning "he can sell her, so surely her work is his" works only for a קטנה. In Step 7 the גמרא uses it to show the פסוק must be teaching about a נערה.)

keyTerms.meaning: just as... so too... (the form of a comparison)
as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: As Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that a daughter's earnings belong to the father?
As it is said:
"And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant"
Just as a maidservant's earnings belong to her master,
so too a daughter's earnings belong to her father.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: מִנַּיִן שֶׁמַּעֲשֵׂה הַבַּת לָאָב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison to the אמה in שמות 21:7: her earnings go to her master, so a daughter's earnings go to her father.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah basis for the father's right to his daughter's earnings, and the rest of the section tests how far it reaches.

steps.title: Maybe this only applies to a young girl the father can sell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: a father can sell only a קטנה, so maybe only her earnings are his, and a נערה keeps her own.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this applies only to a minor girl, whom the father can sell. A young woman, whom he cannot sell, should keep her own earnings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in רב's proof. The comparison to an אמה may only work for a daughter who could actually be sold as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father can sell his daughter as an אמה only while she is a קטנה, under twelve. Once she is a נערה he cannot sell her. If the comparison is tied to selling, a נערה's earnings may be her own.

keyTerms.meaning: a girl under twelve, a minor
a girl from twelve to twelve and a half

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the proof covers every daughter. The question is whether the proof from selling reaches a נערה, who can no longer be sold.

phrases.english: But say that this applies only to a minor girl,
whom he is able to sell;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל נַעֲרָה, דְּלָא מָצֵי מְזַבֵּן לַהּ —
phrases.english: but a young woman, whom he is not able to sell,
her earnings should be her own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far רב's comparison reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's source from the אמה, as applied to a נערה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison depends on the father's power to sell. He has that power only over a קטנה, so a נערה's earnings should be her own.

steps.title: A logical argument from the father handing her over to marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that a נערה's earnings must also be her father's. The Torah lets him hand her over to חופה, and that takes her away from her work.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that they belong to her father. If her earnings were not her father's, how could the Torah give the father the right to hand her over to the wedding canopy? He would be taking her away from her work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the father's right with logic instead of a פסוק. It points to the father's right to marry off his נערה daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father has the right to hand his daughter over to חופה even while she is a נערה. The wedding stops her from working that day. If her earnings were hers, she could object, so the Torah's grant of this right shows her earnings are his.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense, it is logical
the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
the wedding canopy, the final stage of marriage

phrases.english: It makes sense that they belong to her father,
because if you were to think
that her earnings are not her father's,
then what about the right the Torah gives him,
the father, to hand her over to the wedding canopy?
How could he hand her over?
He would be taking her away from her work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about a נערה with a logical argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A logical argument from another right the father has
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נערה cannot be sold, so her earnings should be her own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father may hand her over to חופה even though it takes away her work time, so her earnings must be his.

steps.title: רב אחאי offers three ways around the argument
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי rejects the logical argument. The father could pay her for the lost work, or hand her over at night, or on שבת and יום טוב, when she does not work anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחאי objects: Say the father pays her for the work she loses. Or say he hands her over at night. Or say he hands her over on שבתות and ימים טובים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי knocks down the argument from step 5. He shows the father could hand her over to חופה without taking away anything that belongs to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed the wedding must cost the daughter work time. רב אחאי gives three cases where it costs her nothing: he pays her back, or the wedding is at night, or on a day when work is forbidden. So the father's right to marry her off does not prove her earnings are his.

phrases.english: Rav Achai objects:
Say that he pays her for the work she loses.
phrases.notes: פקעת is literally a ball of thread or yarn, so this is pay for the spinning she misses.

phrases.english: Or say that he hands her over at night.
Or say that he hands her over
on Shabbatot and Festivals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the logical argument of step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the father's right to hand his daughter over to חופה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument assumes the wedding must cost her work. It need not: he can pay her for it, or hold the wedding at night or on שבת or יום טוב.

steps.title: The verse is really teaching about a young woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the אמה פסוק and reads it a new way. A father who may sell a קטנה obviously owns her earnings, so the פסוק must be coming to teach that a נערה's earnings also go to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: for a קטנה we don't need a פסוק. Since her father can even sell her, do we need to be told that her earnings are his? The פסוק was needed only for a נערה.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 6 knocked down the logical proof. So the גמרא comes back to the פסוק and shows that it must be talking about a נערה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא in step 4 said the אמה פסוק covers only a קטנה. The גמרא now flips this around. For a קטנה, no פסוק is needed, because the right to sell her is bigger than the right to her earnings. A פסוק that teaches nothing new about a קטנה must be teaching about a נערה.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it needed? (said when the answer is obviously no)

steps.whatToRemember: A father's right to his daughter's earnings applies to a נערה too. We learn it from the אמה פסוק, because a קטנה would not need a פסוק at all.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not dropping the אמה פסוק here. It is keeping the same פסוק and showing that it must be talking about a נערה.

phrases.english: Rather: a minor girl does not need a verse —
now, if he can actually sell her,
phrases.notes: He means selling her as an אמה, which the Torah allows only while she is a קטנה.

phrases.english: is it necessary to teach about her earnings?!
[Rather,] where the verse was needed was for a young woman.
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets. The meaning is the same either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אחאי's rejection, the גמרא goes back to the original פסוק and uses it to answer the קשיא in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirecting the verse: what is obvious for a קטנה shows that the פסוק must be about a נערה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אמה פסוק teaches only about a קטנה, since only she can be sold.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קטנה needs no פסוק, so the פסוק teaches that a נערה's earnings also belong to her father.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a father cancels her vows?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next right from the משנה, cancelling the daughter's נדרים, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father has the right to cancel her vows. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next item in the משנה and asks where it comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new item on the משנה's list of the father's rights. It is a plain request for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: In nullifying her vows. From where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earnings topic is finished, so the גמרא moves on to the next right in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for a father's right to cancel his daughter's נדרים.

steps.title: The verse about vows made in her father's house
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק about נדרים made by a girl in her youth, while she lives in her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: "In her youth, in her father's house."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from the section on נדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section in במדבר ל teaches the laws of a father cancelling his daughter's נדרים. Its closing words point to the time when she is young and still in her father's house.

phrases.english: As it is written: "In her youth, in her father's house."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "בנעוריה בית אביה" in the section on נדרים.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a father accepts her bill of divorce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next right, that the father accepts his daughter's גט, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he accepts her גט. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next item in the משנה and asks for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is about a girl who was married (through קידושין) while young and then divorced. The משנה says the father can receive the גט for her, and the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: He receives her bill of divorce

phrases.english: And he accepts her bill of divorce. From where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next right listed in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for a father's right to accept his daughter's גט.

steps.title: Leaving a marriage is compared to entering one
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts "she leaves" right next to "she becomes [another man's wife]." This links divorce to קידושין, so the father, who accepts her קידושין, also accepts her גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: "And she leaves… and she becomes." Leaving a marriage is compared to entering one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by putting divorce and marriage side by side, using a פסוק that mentions them together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father has the right to accept קידושין for his daughter. Because the Torah places her "leaving" right beside her "becoming" a wife, the two are treated alike. So whoever can bring her into a marriage can also receive the גט that takes her out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: They are compared to each other (a היקש)

phrases.english: As it is written: "And she leaves… and she becomes,"
phrases.notes: דברים כד:ב. The dots skip the middle words; the end of the פסוק is "another man's wife."

phrases.english: leaving is compared to becoming [a wife].

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש between divorce and קידושין: the father controls her קידושין, so he also receives her גט.
steps.whatToRemember: Divorce works like קידושין (they are compared to each other). Since the father accepts his daughter's קידושין, he also accepts her גט.

steps.title: A dispute over whether a father eats the produce of her property
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the father does not eat the produce of his daughter's property during her lifetime. A ברייתא shows this is argued: תנא קמא says he does not, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he does not eat produce during her lifetime." The Rabbis taught: a father does not eat the produce of his daughter's property during her lifetime. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: a father does eat the produce during his daughter's lifetime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next line and brings a ברייתא showing that תנאים argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה follows תנא קמא: the father gets no produce from property his daughter owns while she is alive. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees and gives the father this right. The next steps will look for the reason behind their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Eats (gets the use of) the produce or profits of property

steps.confusionAlert: "Produce" here does not mean only fruit. It means any profit from the daughter's own property while the property itself still belongs to her.

phrases.english: And he does not eat produce during her lifetime.
The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָאָב אֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת בְּחַיֵּי בִתּוֹ.
phrases.english: The father does not eat produce during his daughter's lifetime.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
The father does eat produce during his daughter's lifetime.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל פֵּירוֹת בְּחַיֶּיהָ. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling in the משנה, which is a limit on the father's rights.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: the father does not eat the produce of his daughter's property during her lifetime. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: he does.

steps.title: What is the reason behind their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea the two תנאים are arguing about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the argument in the ברייתא. It is getting ready to explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the two rulings is not enough. The גמרא wants to find the idea that makes one תנא say yes and the other say no.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute quoted in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The idea that the two opinions in the ברייתא disagree about.

steps.title: The first opinion: a husband gets produce so that he will ransom her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts explaining תנא קמא. A husband was given the produce by the Rabbis, because otherwise he would hold back from ransoming his wife if she were captured. Step 15 finishes this explanation by contrasting the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנא קמא holds: it makes sense for a husband, to whom the Rabbis gave the produce, because otherwise he would hold back and not ransom her…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining תנא קמא's opinion. It compares the father to a husband, and the explanation is not finished yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband's right to the produce is a rabbinic arrangement. Its purpose is to make sure he will pay to ransom his wife if she is captured. The "בשלמא" (granted) wording sets up a contrast: this reason works for a husband, and the גמרא is about to show why it does not work for a father.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא
Granted, it makes sense in this case (sets up a contrast)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a husband's right to the produce comes with an obligation, ransoming his wife. Whether a father has a similar reason is what decides the dispute.

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
Granted, a husband,
the Rabbis instituted produce for him,
because if so, he would hold back and not ransom her,
phrases.notes: "If so" means if the Rabbis hadn't given him the produce. Then he might not pay to free her if she were captured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question in step 13 by explaining תנא קמא's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first half of the explanation: a husband gets the produce so that he will ransom his wife. The contrast with a father comes next.

steps.title: A father will ransom his daughter anyway
steps.stepSummary: תנא קמא's reasoning ends: the produce was given to a husband so he would not hold back from ransoming her, but a father will ransom his daughter without any reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a father, what can you say? That he will hold back and not ransom her? Even without this, he will ransom her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why תנא קמא says the father does not eat the produce. A father will ransom his own daughter even without getting anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14 we learned the Rabbis gave the husband the produce so he would not hold back from ransoming his wife. That reason does not apply to a father, because he loves his daughter and will ransom her anyway. So there is no reason to give him the produce.

phrases.english: But a father, what is there to say
That he will hold back and not ransom her?
Even without this he will ransom her!
phrases.notes: "This" means the right to eat her produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of תנא קמא's view that was started in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What idea are the תנאים arguing about?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to תנא קמא, the reason for giving produce (so he will ransom her) does not apply to a father, who will ransom her anyway.

steps.title: Even a father might tell her to ransom herself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that a father, too, might hold back, thinking his daughter has her own money to ransom herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds: a father also might hold back and not ransom her. He thinks: she has a pouch of money in her hand, let her go and ransom herself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other side. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says even a father might not ransom her if he gets nothing from her property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter owns property, so the father may think: let her use her own money. So the same reason that gives the husband the produce also applies to the father. That is why the father eats the produce too.

keyTerms.meaning: a pouch, a purse of money

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on the reason: produce is given so the person will ransom her. They only argue whether a father needs this push. תנא קמא says no, so he does not eat the produce. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says yes, so he does.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda holds:
A father also holds back and does not ransom her.
He thinks: a pouch is held in her hand,
phrases.notes: He means she has her own money set aside.

phrases.english: let her go and ransom herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reasoning to the one in Step 15, finishing the answer to Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a father might also hold back, so he too is given the produce.

steps.title: Does the husband get the dowry if the bride dies during אירוסין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that a married husband has more rights than the father. It then brings a ברייתא: if the father promised a dowry and the bride died during אירוסין, תנא קמא says the husband gets nothing, and רבי נתן says he gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she married, the husband has more than the father, since he eats the produce, etc. The Rabbis taught: if he wrote for her produce, clothing and vessels that would come with her from her father's house to her husband's house, and she died, the husband did not acquire these things. In the name of רבי נתן they said: the husband did acquire these things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about the husband. It brings a ברייתא with an argument about the dowry when a bride dies before the wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father promised a dowry that would go with her to her husband's house. She died during אירוסין, before she got there. תנא קמא says the husband gets nothing, and רבי נתן says he gets it.

phrases.english: If she married, the husband has more than him
phrases.notes: "Him" is the father. This is a quote from our משנה.

phrases.english: in that he eats, etc.
The Rabbis taught: If he wrote for her produce,
clothing and vessels that would come with her
from her father's house to her husband's house
and she died, the husband did not acquire
phrases.notes: She died during אירוסין, before she moved into his house.

phrases.english: these things.
In the name of Rabbi Natan they said:
The husband did acquire these things.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיסֵּת, יָתֵר עָלָיו הַבַּעַל שֶׁהוּא אוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the father's rights to the next line of the משנה, about the husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a bride dies during אירוסין, תנא קמא says the husband does not get the promised dowry. רבי נתן says he does.

steps.title: Is this the same argument as the one about collecting a כתובה after אירוסין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא's argument matches the argument between רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the Rabbis. The Rabbis say a woman widowed or divorced even from אירוסין collects her whole כתובה. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says after אירוסין she collects only the basic amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about the same thing as רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the Rabbis? As we learned: if she was widowed or divorced, whether from נשואין or from אירוסין, she collects everything. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: from נשואין she collects everything, but from אירוסין a virgin collects two hundred and a widow a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the argument in the ברייתא is really an older argument from a different משנה. This step sets up the comparison, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both arguments ask the same thing: do promises made at אירוסין count right away, or only once the marriage happens? The Rabbis let her collect the extra amounts even from אירוסין, which looks like רבי נתן. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the extras were promised only for the sake of the marriage, which looks like תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.confusionAlert: "Collects everything" means the whole כתובה, including any extra the husband added. It does not just mean the basic amount set by the Rabbis.
